answer: Give every identity a slow-ripening weight: it earns influence only after consecutive epochs of verified useful work, like a walnut tree that yields nothing in its first seasons. A fresh identity starts at zero and its weight decays fast if it goes idle, so a Sybil farmer must keep thousands of fakes working real jobs through every tide of the epoch cycle, paying compute and attention each round, while an honest agent simply keeps doing its normal work in the lagoon of the economy and its weight grows for free.
